title: First 30 days
summary: Pass card in hand, Singpass live, bank open, longer housing underway. This is when Singapore starts to feel operational.

items.title: Collect / confirm your EP or Dependant Pass card
items.detail: Photograph both sides once it arrives (password vault, not a group chat). Set up the SGWorkPass app with your digital work pass. Update your mobile number with MOM if HR used a temporary SIM earlier. Lost/stolen plastic → HR files MOM replacement within 1 week.

items.title: Activate Singpass (and Singpass Face if offered)
items.detail: FIN holders 15+ can register. Use your Singapore mobile for SMS 2FA if your registered address is local. Wrong form fields can force a mail-PIN delay — double-check FIN and issue dates from SGWorkPass / notification documents.

items.title: Open a local bank account
items.detail: DBS, OCBC, UOB, and Standard Chartered are common. Bring passport, physical pass, employment letter, and proof of address. Singpass + MyInfo makes online opening far easier once biometrics are done.

items.title: Register PayNow to your FIN / local number
items.detail: Link PayNow after the account is live. Prefer FIN over a recycled mobile number when the bank offers both. If you mistype a proxy, call your bank for erroneous-transfer recovery — never peer-refund strangers.

items.title: If bringing pets — confirm AVS schedule / AQC booking
items.detail: Match the pet’s export country to AVS Schedule I–III. Book AQC via QMS when quarantine applies; file the import licence as owner or via an AVS-recognised agent. Housing pet clauses must be in writing.

items.title: Confirm CPF / levy status with HR
items.detail: Most EP holders do not contribute to CPF. Know what is deducted and what is not so salary slips make sense.

items.title: Start the longer-term housing search
items.detail: Decide condo vs HDB eligibility, budget, and agent engagement. Sketch first-month cash (deposit + advance rent + stamp duty + agent) before you LOI — use the lease-duty tool if you only need the IRAS line item. If the TA has a diplomatic clause, sketch lock-in + notice dates on /tools/lease-notice before you assume an early exit is free.

items.title: If the TA has a diplomatic clause — sketch lock-in dates
items.detail: Common 24-month TAs allow written notice after a 12-month lock-in with ~2 months’ notice — only if your clause says so. Run the dates before you rely on early exit when resigning later.

items.title: Move onto a proper telco plan
items.detail: Port your prepaid number to postpaid or a longer prepaid once your address is stable enough for billing.

items.title: Enquire at shortlisted schools (if with kids)
items.detail: International-school waitlists and fixed admissions rounds (e.g. UWCSEA Sep–Nov for the following August) move slowly. Watch the calendar for AEIS/S-AEIS, P1, and IS application windows — AEIS tests are only held in Singapore.

items.title: Register with a GP and review insurance
items.detail: Confirm inpatient vs outpatient cover, panel clinics, and maternity/mental-health riders if relevant.

items.title: Start foreign licence conversion before month 12
items.detail: Foreigners residing here generally get under 12 months on a foreign licence (+ IDP / English translation rules). Conversion usually needs BTT while still inside that window — calendar the clock from your arrival date, not from when you buy a car.

items.title: Book one social or club intro
items.detail: A chamber mixer, nationality association coffee, or hash run. Belonging is a 30-day problem, not a year-three problem.
